passages.text: A Maskil of Asaph.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
Asaph was a leader and musician in Israel.
This psalm is a maskil.
A maskil is a song or poem meant to teach wisdom.

passages.text: Give ear, O my people, to my instruction; listen to the words of my mouth.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
He was wise.
He spoke to the people of Israel.
He said, “My people, listen to my teaching.”
He said, “Pay attention to the words I speak.”
passages.original: מַשְׂכִּ֗יל לְאָ֫סָ֥ף הַאֲזִ֣ינָה עַ֭מִּי תּוֹרָתִ֑י הַטּ֥וּ אָ֝זְנְכֶ֗ם לְאִמְרֵי־ פִֽי׃

passages.text: I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the beginning, that we have heard and known and our fathers have relayed to us.
passages.sermon:
Asaph is the writer.
Asaph is giving a teaching.
Asaph says, "I will speak in parables."
A parable is a story with a lesson.
Asaph says, "I will tell things that were hidden from the beginning."
These things are not new.
We have heard these things before.
We know these things.
Our fathers told these things to us.
Our ancestors passed these lessons down to us.
passages.original: אֶפְתְּחָ֣ה בְמָשָׁ֣ל פִּ֑י אַבִּ֥יעָה חִ֝יד֗וֹת מִנִּי־ קֶֽדֶם׃ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁ֭מַעְנוּ וַנֵּדָעֵ֑ם וַ֝אֲבוֹתֵ֗ינוּ סִפְּרוּ־ לָֽנוּ׃

passages.text: We will not hide them from their children, but will declare to the next generation the praises of the LORD and His might, and the wonders He has performed.
passages.sermon:
We will not hide these things from their children.
We will tell the next generation.
We will declare the praises of the LORD.
We will speak of His power.
We will tell of the wonders He has done.
passages.original: לֹ֤א נְכַחֵ֨ד׀ מִבְּנֵיהֶ֗ם לְד֥וֹר אַחֲר֗וֹן מְֽ֭סַפְּרִים תְּהִלּ֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה וֶעֱזוּז֥וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָֽׂה׃

passages.text: For He established a testimony in Jacob and appointed a law in Israel, which He commanded our fathers to teach to their children, that the coming generation would know them— even children yet to be born— to arise and tell their own children that they should put their confidence in God, not forgetting His works, but keeping His commandments.
passages.sermon:
God gave a testimony to Jacob.
God set a law in Israel.
God commanded our ancestors to teach these things to their children.
God wanted the next generation to know His testimony and law.
Even children not yet born would learn them.
These children would grow up and teach their own children.
God wanted each generation to put their trust in Him.
God wanted them to remember His works.
God wanted them to obey His commandments.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤קֶם עֵד֨וּת׀ בְּֽיַעֲקֹ֗ב וְתוֹרָה֮ שָׂ֤ם בְּיִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִ֭וָּה אֶת־ אֲבוֹתֵ֑ינוּ לְ֝הוֹדִיעָ֗ם לִבְנֵיהֶֽם׃ לְמַ֤עַן יֵדְע֨וּ׀ דּ֣וֹר אַ֭חֲרוֹן בָּנִ֣ים יִוָּלֵ֑דוּ יָ֝קֻ֗מוּ וִֽיסַפְּר֥וּ לִבְנֵיהֶֽם׃ וְיָשִׂ֥ימוּ בֵֽאלֹהִ֗ים כִּ֫סְלָ֥ם וְלֹ֣א יִ֭שְׁכְּחוּ מַֽעַלְלֵי־ אֵ֑ל וּמִצְוֺתָ֥יו יִנְצֹֽרוּ׃

passages.text: Then they will not be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, whose heart was not loyal, whose spirit was not faithful to God.
passages.sermon:
God wants the next generation to be different from their fathers.
Their fathers were stubborn.
Their fathers were rebellious.
Their fathers did not prepare their hearts for God.
Their fathers did not stay faithful to God.
God wants the next generation to be loyal to Him.
God wants the next generation to be faithful in spirit.
passages.original: וְלֹ֤א יִהְי֨וּ׀ כַּאֲבוֹתָ֗ם דּוֹר֮ סוֹרֵ֪ר וּמֹ֫רֶ֥ה דּ֭וֹר לֹא־ הֵכִ֣ין לִבּ֑וֹ וְלֹא־ נֶאֶמְנָ֖ה אֶת־ אֵ֣ל רוּחֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The archers of Ephraim turned back on the day of battle.
passages.sermon:
The tribe of Ephraim had skilled archers.
They carried bows.
They faced a day of battle.
They turned back during the battle.
passages.original: בְּֽנֵי־ אֶפְרַ֗יִם נוֹשְׁקֵ֥י רוֹמֵי־ קָ֑שֶׁת הָ֝פְכ֗וּ בְּי֣וֹם קְרָֽב׃

passages.text: They failed to keep God’s covenant and refused to live by His law.
passages.sermon: The people did not keep God's covenant.\r\nThey refused to follow God's law.
passages.original: לֹ֣א שָׁ֭מְרוּ בְּרִ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים וּ֝בְתוֹרָת֗וֹ מֵאֲנ֥וּ לָלֶֽכֶת׃

passages.text: They forgot what He had done, the wonders He had shown them.
passages.sermon:
The people forgot God’s deeds.
They did not remember what God had done.
God had shown them His wonders.
They forgot the wonders God showed them.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכְּח֥וּ עֲלִילוֹתָ֑יו וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶרְאָֽם׃

passages.text: He worked wonders before their fathers in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
He did amazing things.
He showed these wonders to the ancestors of Israel.
He did this in Egypt.
He did this in the region called Zoan.
passages.original: נֶ֣גֶד אֲ֭בוֹתָם עָ֣שָׂה פֶ֑לֶא בְּאֶ֖רֶץ מִצְרַ֣יִם שְׂדֵה־ צֹֽעַן׃

passages.text: He split the sea and brought them through; He set the waters upright like a wall.
passages.sermon:
God led the people of Israel out of Egypt.
He split the sea.
He made a path through the sea.
He brought the people safely through the sea.
He made the waters stand upright like a wall.
passages.original: בָּ֣קַע יָ֭ם וַיַּֽעֲבִירֵ֑ם וַֽיַּצֶּב־ מַ֥יִם כְּמוֹ־ נֵֽד׃

passages.text: He led them with a cloud by day and with a light of fire all night.
passages.sermon:
God led the Israelites.
He used a cloud during the day.
He used a light of fire at night.
He guided them at all times.
passages.original: וַיַּנְחֵ֣ם בֶּעָנָ֣ן יוֹמָ֑ם וְכָל־ הַ֝לַּ֗יְלָה בְּא֣וֹר אֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: He split the rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink as abundant as the seas.
passages.sermon:
God led the Israelites in the wilderness.
He split the rocks in the wilderness.
He gave the Israelites water to drink.
He gave them water in great abundance.
The water was as abundant as the seas.
passages.original: יְבַקַּ֣ע צֻ֭רִים בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַ֝יַּ֗שְׁקְ כִּתְהֹמ֥וֹת רַבָּֽה׃

passages.text: He brought streams from the stone and made water flow down like rivers.
passages.sermon:
God acted in the wilderness.
God brought streams from a stone.
God made water flow down like rivers.
God provided water for the people.
passages.original: וַיּוֹצִ֣א נוֹזְלִ֣ים מִסָּ֑לַע וַיּ֖וֹרֶד כַּנְּהָר֣וֹת מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: But they continued to sin against Him, rebelling in the desert against the Most High.
passages.sermon:
The people were in the desert.
God is the Most High.
The people sinned against God.
They did not stop sinning.
They rebelled against the Most High.
They did this while they were in the desert.
passages.original: וַיּוֹסִ֣יפוּ ע֭וֹד לַחֲטֹא־ ל֑וֹ לַֽמְר֥וֹת עֶ֝לְי֗וֹן בַּצִּיָּֽה׃

passages.text: They willfully tested God by demanding the food they craved.
passages.sermon:
The people were in the desert.
They wanted food for themselves.
They tested God in their hearts.
They demanded the food they craved.
passages.original: וַיְנַסּוּ־ אֵ֥ל בִּלְבָבָ֑ם לִֽשְׁאָל־ אֹ֥כֶל לְנַפְשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: They spoke against God, saying, “Can God really prepare a table in the wilderness?
passages.sermon: The people of Israel spoke against God.\r\nThey questioned God’s power.\r\nThey said, “Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?”
passages.original: וַֽיְדַבְּר֗וּ בֵּֽאלֹ֫הִ֥ים אָ֭מְרוּ הֲי֣וּכַל אֵ֑ל לַעֲרֹ֥ךְ שֻׁ֝לְחָ֗ן בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: When He struck the rock, water gushed out and torrents raged. But can He also give bread or supply His people with meat?”
passages.sermon:
God struck the rock.
Water gushed out from the rock.
Streams flowed in abundance.
The people questioned God.
They asked if God could also give them bread.
They wondered if God could provide meat for His people.
passages.original: הֵ֤ן הִכָּה־ צ֨וּר׀ וַיָּז֣וּבוּ מַיִם֮ וּנְחָלִ֪ים יִ֫שְׁטֹ֥פוּ הֲגַם־ לֶ֭חֶם י֣וּכַל תֵּ֑ת אִם־ יָכִ֖ין שְׁאֵ֣ר לְעַמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Therefore the LORD heard and was filled with wrath; so a fire was kindled against Jacob, and His anger flared against Israel, because they did not believe God or rely on His salvation.
passages.sermon:
The LORD heard the people.
The people did not believe God.
The people did not trust in God's salvation.
The LORD became very angry.
He showed His wrath against Jacob.
He sent fire against Jacob.
His anger rose against Israel.
passages.original: לָכֵ֤ן׀ שָׁמַ֥ע יְהוָ֗ה וַֽיִּתְעַבָּ֥ר וְ֭אֵשׁ נִשְּׂקָ֣ה בְיַעֲקֹ֑ב וְגַם־ אַ֝֗ף עָלָ֥ה בְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ כִּ֤י לֹ֣א הֶ֭אֱמִינוּ בֵּאלֹהִ֑ים וְלֹ֥א בָ֝טְח֗וּ בִּֽישׁוּעָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Yet He commanded the clouds above and opened the doors of the heavens.
passages.sermon: God acted with power and authority.\r\nGod gave a command to the clouds above.\r\nGod opened the doors of the heavens.
passages.original: וַיְצַ֣ו שְׁחָקִ֣ים מִמָּ֑עַל וְדַלְתֵ֖י שָׁמַ֣יִם פָּתָֽח׃

passages.text: He rained down manna for them to eat; He gave them grain from heaven.
passages.sermon:
God cared for the people of Israel in the wilderness.
God sent food from heaven.
God made manna fall for them to eat.
God gave them grain from above.
passages.original: וַיַּמְטֵ֬ר עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם מָ֣ן לֶאֱכֹ֑ל וּדְגַן־ שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם נָ֣תַן לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: Man ate the bread of angels; He sent them food in abundance.
passages.sermon:
God provided food for the people of Israel in the wilderness.
He gave them bread that angels eat.
People ate this special bread.
God sent them plenty of food.
They had enough to be satisfied.
passages.original: לֶ֣חֶם אַ֭בִּירִים אָ֣כַל אִ֑ישׁ צֵידָ֬ה שָׁלַ֖ח לָהֶ֣ם לָשֹֽׂבַע׃

passages.text: He stirred the east wind from the heavens and drove the south wind by His might.
passages.sermon: God acted with great power.\r\nGod stirred the east wind in the sky.\r\nGod drove the south wind with His strength.
passages.original: יַסַּ֣ע קָ֭דִים בַּשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיְנַהֵ֖ג בְּעֻזּ֣וֹ תֵימָֽן׃

passages.text: He rained meat on them like dust, and winged birds like the sand of the sea.
passages.sermon:
God acted with great power.
God sent meat down from above.
The meat fell on the people like dust falls to the ground.
God also sent birds with wings.
The birds were as many as the sand by the sea.
passages.original: וַיַּמְטֵ֬ר עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּעָפָ֣ר שְׁאֵ֑ר וּֽכְח֥וֹל יַ֝מִּ֗ים ע֣וֹף כָּנָֽף׃

passages.text: He felled them in the midst of their camp, all around their dwellings.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
God caused the birds to fall.
The birds fell in the middle of the Israelites’ camp.
The birds fell all around their homes.
passages.original: וַ֭יַּפֵּל בְּקֶ֣רֶב מַחֲנֵ֑הוּ סָ֝בִ֗יב לְמִשְׁכְּנֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: So they ate and were well filled, for He gave them what they craved.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel ate the food.
They became very full.
God gave them what they wanted.
God satisfied their craving.
passages.original: וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ וַיִּשְׂבְּע֣וּ מְאֹ֑ד וְ֝תַֽאֲוָתָ֗ם יָבִ֥א לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Yet before they had filled their desire, with the food still in their mouths, God’s anger flared against them, and He put to death their strongest and subdued the young men of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel ate the food they craved.
They had not finished their desire.
The food was still in their mouths.
God became angry with them.
God killed their strongest people.
God brought down the young men of Israel.
passages.original: לֹא־ זָר֥וּ מִתַּאֲוָתָ֑ם ע֝֗וֹד אָכְלָ֥ם בְּפִיהֶֽם׃ וְאַ֤ף אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀ עָ֘לָ֤ה בָהֶ֗ם וַֽ֭יַּהֲרֹג בְּמִשְׁמַנֵּיהֶ֑ם וּבַחוּרֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל הִכְרִֽיעַ׃

passages.text: In spite of all this, they kept on sinning; despite His wonderful works, they did not believe.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel saw God’s wonderful works.
God showed them many miracles.
Still, they did not believe God.
They kept on sinning.
They did not trust Him, even after all He did.
passages.original: בְּכָל־ זֹ֭את חָֽטְאוּ־ ע֑וֹד וְלֹֽא־ הֶ֝אֱמִ֗ינוּ בְּנִפְלְאוֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: So He ended their days in futility, and their years in sudden terror.
passages.sermon: God acted with judgment.\r\nHe made their days empty and meaningless.\r\nHe caused their years to end quickly and with fear.
passages.original: וַיְכַל־ בַּהֶ֥בֶל יְמֵיהֶ֑ם וּ֝שְׁנוֹתָ֗ם בַּבֶּהָלָֽה׃

passages.text: When He slew them, they would seek Him; they repented and searched for God.
passages.sermon:
God punished the people by killing some of them.
After this, the people began to seek God.
They turned back to God.
They searched for God.
passages.original: אִם־ הֲרָגָ֥ם וּדְרָשׁ֑וּהוּ וְ֝שָׁ֗בוּ וְשִֽׁחֲרוּ־ אֵֽל׃

passages.text: And they remembered that God was their Rock, that God Most High was their Redeemer.
passages.sermon:
The people remembered God.  
God was their Rock.  
God Most High was their Redeemer.
passages.original: וַֽ֭יִּזְכְּרוּ כִּֽי־ אֱלֹהִ֣ים צוּרָ֑ם וְאֵ֥ל עֶ֝לְיוֹן גֹּאֲלָֽם׃

passages.text: But they deceived Him with their mouths, and lied to Him with their tongues.
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to God with their mouths.
They tried to deceive God with their words.
They lied to God with their tongues.
They did not speak truthfully to Him.
passages.original: וַיְפַתּ֥וּהוּ בְּפִיהֶ֑ם וּ֝בִלְשׁוֹנָ֗ם יְכַזְּבוּ־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Their hearts were disloyal to Him, and they were unfaithful to His covenant.
passages.sermon: The people did not have loyal hearts toward God.\r\nThey were not faithful to God's covenant.
passages.original: וְ֭לִבָּם לֹא־ נָכ֣וֹן עִמּ֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א נֶ֝אֶמְנ֗וּ בִּבְרִיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And yet He was compassionate; He forgave their iniquity and did not destroy them. He often restrained His anger and did not unleash His full wrath.
passages.sermon:
God is compassionate.
God forgives iniquity.
God does not destroy them.
God often restrains His anger.
God does not unleash His full wrath.
passages.original: וְה֤וּא רַח֨וּם׀ יְכַפֵּ֥ר עָוֺן֮ וְֽלֹא־ יַ֫שְׁחִ֥ית וְ֭הִרְבָּה לְהָשִׁ֣יב אַפּ֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־ יָ֝עִיר כָּל־ חֲמָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He remembered that they were but flesh, a passing breeze that does not return.
passages.sermon:
God remembered the people of Israel.
He saw that they were only flesh.
They were weak and mortal.
They were like a passing breeze.
The breeze goes away and does not return.
passages.original: וַ֭יִּזְכֹּר כִּי־ בָשָׂ֣ר הֵ֑מָּה ר֥וּחַ ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ וְלֹ֣א יָשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: How often they disobeyed Him in the wilderness and grieved Him in the desert!
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel were in the wilderness.
They disobeyed God many times there.
They grieved God in the desert.
They caused Him sorrow again and again.
passages.original: כַּ֭מָּה יַמְר֣וּהוּ בַמִּדְבָּ֑ר יַ֝עֲצִיב֗וּהוּ בִּֽישִׁימֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Again and again they tested God and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
passages.sermon: The people of Israel tested God many times.\r\nThey provoked the Holy One of Israel again and again.
passages.original: וַיָּשׁ֣וּבוּ וַיְנַסּ֣וּ אֵ֑ל וּקְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל הִתְווּ׃

passages.text: They did not remember His power — the day He redeemed them from the adversary, when He performed His signs in Egypt and His wonders in the fields of Zoan.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel did not remember God's power.
God redeemed them from their enemies.
God did this on a certain day.
God performed signs in Egypt.
God showed wonders in the fields of Zoan.
passages.original: לֹא־ זָכְר֥וּ אֶת־ יָד֑וֹ י֝֗וֹם אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־ פָּדָ֥ם מִנִּי־ צָֽר׃ אֲשֶׁר־ שָׂ֣ם בְּ֭מִצְרַיִם אֹֽתוֹתָ֑יו וּ֝מוֹפְתָ֗יו בִּשְׂדֵה־ צֹֽעַן׃

passages.text: He turned their rivers to blood, and from their streams they could not drink.
passages.sermon:
God acted with great power.
God turned the rivers of Egypt into blood.
The people of Egypt saw their rivers become blood.
The streams in Egypt also became blood.
The Egyptians could not drink from their rivers.
The Egyptians could not drink from their streams.
passages.original: וַיַּהֲפֹ֣ךְ לְ֭דָם יְאֹרֵיהֶ֑ם וְ֝נֹזְלֵיהֶ֗ם בַּל־ יִשְׁתָּיֽוּן׃

passages.text: He sent swarms of flies that devoured them, and frogs that devastated them.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
God sent swarms of flies against the Egyptians.
The flies devoured the Egyptians.
God also sent frogs against the Egyptians.
The frogs devastated the Egyptians.
passages.original: יְשַׁלַּ֬ח בָּהֶ֣ם עָ֭רֹב וַיֹּאכְלֵ֑ם וּ֝צְפַרְדֵּ֗עַ וַתַּשְׁחִיתֵֽם׃

passages.text: He gave their crops to the grasshopper, the fruit of their labor to the locust.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
God gave their crops to the grasshopper.
God gave the fruit of their labor to the locust.
The grasshopper ate their crops.
The locust destroyed what they worked for.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לֶחָסִ֣יל יְבוּלָ֑ם וִֽ֝יגִיעָ֗ם לָאַרְבֶּֽה׃

passages.text: He killed their vines with hailstones and their sycamore-figs with sleet.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
He sent hailstones.
The hailstones struck their vineyards.
The hailstones killed their grapevines.
God also sent sleet.
The sleet struck their sycamore-fig trees.
The sleet destroyed their sycamore-figs.
passages.original: יַהֲרֹ֣ג בַּבָּרָ֣ד גַּפְנָ֑ם וְ֝שִׁקְמוֹתָ֗ם בַּֽחֲנָמַֽל׃

passages.text: He abandoned their cattle to the hail and their livestock to bolts of lightning.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power in Egypt.
He gave their cattle to the hail.
He gave their livestock to bolts of lightning.
God did not protect their animals.
God allowed destruction to come through hail and lightning.
passages.original: וַיַּסְגֵּ֣ר לַבָּרָ֣ד בְּעִירָ֑ם וּ֝מִקְנֵיהֶ֗ם לָרְשָׁפִֽים׃

passages.text: He unleashed His fury against them, wrath, indignation, and calamity— a band of destroying angels.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
God sent His fury against the Egyptians.
He showed wrath.
He showed indignation.
He brought calamity.
He sent a group of destroying angels.
passages.original: יְשַׁלַּח־ בָּ֨ם׀ חֲר֬וֹן אַפּ֗וֹ עֶבְרָ֣ה וָזַ֣עַם וְצָרָ֑ה מִ֝שְׁלַ֗חַת מַלְאֲכֵ֥י רָעִֽים׃

passages.text: He cleared a path for His anger; He did not spare them from death but delivered their lives to the plague.
passages.sermon:
God acted with anger against the Egyptians.
God made a way for His anger to reach them.
God did not protect their lives from death.
God gave their lives over to the plague.
passages.original: יְפַלֵּ֥ס נָתִ֗יב לְאַ֫פּ֥וֹ לֹא־ חָשַׂ֣ךְ מִמָּ֣וֶת נַפְשָׁ֑ם וְ֝חַיָּתָ֗ם לַדֶּ֥בֶר הִסְגִּֽיר׃

passages.text: He struck all the firstborn of Egypt, the virility in the tents of Ham.
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
\r\nGod struck every firstborn in Egypt.
\r\nGod struck the first and strongest sons.
\r\nThese sons lived in the tents of Ham.
\r\nHam’s descendants lived in Egypt.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣ךְ כָּל־ בְּכ֣וֹר בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם רֵאשִׁ֥ית א֝וֹנִ֗ים בְּאָהֳלֵי־ חָֽם׃

passages.text: He led out His people like sheep and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
God led His people.
He treated them like sheep.
He guided them like a flock.
He led them in the wilderness.
passages.original: וַיַּסַּ֣ע כַּצֹּ֣אן עַמּ֑וֹ וַֽיְנַהֲגֵ֥ם כַּ֝עֵ֗דֶר בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: He led them safely, so they did not fear, but the sea engulfed their enemies.
passages.sermon: God led His people safely.\r\nThey did not feel fear.\r\nThe sea covered their enemies.
passages.original: וַיַּנְחֵ֣ם לָ֭בֶטַח וְלֹ֣א פָחָ֑דוּ וְאֶת־ א֝וֹיְבֵיהֶ֗ם כִּסָּ֥ה הַיָּֽם׃

passages.text: He brought them to His holy land, to the mountain His right hand had acquired.
passages.sermon:
God led His people.
He brought them to His holy land.
This land was special to God.
God’s right hand acquired a mountain for them.
God gave this mountain to His people.
passages.original: וַ֭יְבִיאֵם אֶל־ גְּב֣וּל קָדְשׁ֑וֹ הַר־ זֶ֝֗ה קָנְתָ֥ה יְמִינֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He drove out nations before them and apportioned their inheritance; He settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
passages.sermon:
God acted for the people of Israel.
God drove out the nations that lived before Israel.
God gave Israel their inheritance.
God divided the land among the tribes of Israel.
God settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
passages.original: וַיְגָ֤רֶשׁ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֨ם׀ גּוֹיִ֗ם וַֽ֭יַּפִּילֵם בְּחֶ֣בֶל נַחֲלָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֥ן בְּ֝אָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: But they tested and disobeyed God Most High, for they did not keep His decrees.
passages.sermon: The people of Israel tested God Most High.\r\nThey disobeyed Him.\r\nThey did not keep His decrees.
passages.original: וַיְנַסּ֣וּ וַ֭יַּמְרוּ אֶת־ אֱלֹהִ֣ים עֶלְי֑וֹן וְ֝עֵדוֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א שָׁמָֽרוּ׃

passages.text: They turned back and were faithless like their fathers, twisted like a faulty bow.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel turned back from God.
They acted with faithlessness.
Their fathers also acted with faithlessness.
The people became twisted.
They were like a faulty bow.
passages.original: וַיִּסֹּ֣גוּ וַֽ֭יִּבְגְּדוּ כַּאֲבוֹתָ֑ם נֶ֝הְפְּכ֗וּ כְּקֶ֣שֶׁת רְמִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: They enraged Him with their high places and provoked His jealousy with their idols.
passages.sermon:
The people angered God Most High.
They did this by using their high places.
They made God jealous.
They did this with their idols.
passages.original: וַיַּכְעִיס֥וּהוּ בְּבָמוֹתָ֑ם וּ֝בִפְסִילֵיהֶ֗ם יַקְנִיאֽוּהוּ׃

passages.text: On hearing it, God was furious and rejected Israel completely.
passages.sermon: God heard what happened.\r\nGod became furious.\r\nGod rejected Israel completely.
passages.original: שָׁמַ֣ע אֱ֭לֹהִים וַֽיִּתְעַבָּ֑ר וַיִּמְאַ֥ס מְ֝אֹ֗ד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among men.
passages.sermon:
God is the subject.
God abandoned the tabernacle at Shiloh.
God had set up this tent among people.
God left the place where He once lived with men.

passages.text: He delivered His strength to captivity, and His splendor to the hand of the adversary.
passages.sermon: God acted with anger toward Israel.\r\nGod gave His strength into captivity.\r\nGod placed His splendor in the hand of the enemy.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לַשְּׁבִ֣י עֻזּ֑וֹ וְֽתִפְאַרְתּ֥וֹ בְיַד־ צָֽר׃

passages.text: He surrendered His people to the sword because He was enraged by His heritage.
passages.sermon:
God became angry with His people.
God’s people were His special possession.
God handed His people over to the sword.
God allowed His people to be attacked and defeated.
passages.original: וַיַּסְגֵּ֣ר לַחֶ֣רֶב עַמּ֑וֹ וּ֝בְנַחֲלָת֗וֹ הִתְעַבָּֽר׃

passages.text: Fire consumed His young men, and their maidens were left without wedding songs.
passages.sermon: God punished His people.\r\nFire destroyed the young men.\r\nThe young women did not celebrate with wedding songs.
passages.original: בַּחוּרָ֥יו אָֽכְלָה־ אֵ֑שׁ וּ֝בְתוּלֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א הוּלָּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: His priests fell by the sword, but their widows could not lament.
passages.sermon: God’s priests died by the sword.\r\nTheir wives became widows.\r\nThe widows could not weep for them.
passages.original: כֹּ֭הֲנָיו בַּחֶ֣רֶב נָפָ֑לוּ וְ֝אַלְמְנֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִבְכֶּֽינָה׃

passages.text: Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a mighty warrior overcome by wine.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the subject.
The Lord seemed to be sleeping.
Then the Lord woke up.
He woke up suddenly.
He was like a strong warrior.
The warrior had been overcome by wine.
The Lord became alert and active.
passages.original: וַיִּקַ֖ץ כְּיָשֵׁ֥ן׀ אֲדֹנָ֑י כְּ֝גִבּ֗וֹר מִתְרוֹנֵ֥ן מִיָּֽיִן׃

passages.text: He beat back His foes; He put them to everlasting shame.
passages.sermon:
The Lord acted with power.
He defeated His enemies.
He drove His foes backward.
He brought everlasting shame upon them.
His judgment was final and lasting.
passages.original: וַיַּךְ־ צָרָ֥יו אָח֑וֹר חֶרְפַּ֥ת ע֝וֹלָ֗ם נָ֣תַן לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: He rejected the tent of Joseph and refused the tribe of Ephraim.
passages.sermon:
God acted with purpose and authority.
God rejected the tent of Joseph.
God did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.
God made a clear decision about His people.
passages.original: וַ֭יִּמְאַס בְּאֹ֣הֶל יוֹסֵ֑ף וּֽבְשֵׁ֥בֶט אֶ֝פְרַ֗יִם לֹ֣א בָחָֽר׃

passages.text: But He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which He loved.
passages.sermon:
God made a choice.
He chose the tribe of Judah.
God also chose Mount Zion.
God loved Mount Zion.
passages.original: וַ֭יִּבְחַר אֶת־ שֵׁ֣בֶט יְהוּדָ֑ה אֶֽת־ הַ֥ר צִ֝יּ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָהֵֽב׃

passages.text: He built His sanctuary like the heights, like the earth He has established forever.
passages.sermon:
God built His sanctuary.
He made it high like the mountains.
He made it strong and lasting like the earth.
God established the earth forever.
He made His sanctuary to last forever.
passages.original: וַיִּ֣בֶן כְּמוֹ־ רָ֭מִים מִקְדָּשׁ֑וֹ כְּ֝אֶ֗רֶץ יְסָדָ֥הּ לְעוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: He chose David His servant and took him from the sheepfolds; from tending the ewes He brought him to be shepherd of His people Jacob, of Israel His inheritance.
passages.sermon:
God chose David.
David was God's servant.
God took David from the sheepfolds.
David was tending the ewes.
God brought David from tending the ewes.
God made David shepherd His people.
God's people are Jacob.
Israel is God's inheritance.
God made David shepherd Israel.
passages.original: וַ֭יִּבְחַר בְּדָוִ֣ד עַבְדּ֑וֹ וַ֝יִּקָּחֵ֗הוּ מִֽמִּכְלְאֹ֥ת צֹֽאן׃ מֵאַחַ֥ר עָל֗וֹת הֱ֫בִיא֥וֹ לִ֭רְעוֹת בְּיַעֲקֹ֣ב עַמּ֑וֹ וּ֝בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So David shepherded them with integrity of heart and guided them with skillful hands.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
God chose David to lead His people.
David cared for the people of Israel.
David led them with a pure and honest heart.
David guided them with wise and skillful hands.
passages.original: וַ֭יִּרְעֵם כְּתֹ֣ם לְבָב֑וֹ וּבִתְבוּנ֖וֹת כַּפָּ֣יו יַנְחֵֽם׃
